RagShortTexts: In 1264 Mudejar Muslims revolted across Andalusia and Murcia, secretly backed by Granada.

Variants.Content: Triggered in 1264 by Alfonso X's forced deportations, the Mudéjar population of Andalusia and Murcia rose in a massive, coordinated rebellion secretly stoked by Muhammad I of Granada and Marinid volunteers. Christian garrisons at Jerez were massacred and Murcia slipped from royal control.

Overwhelmed by simultaneous uprisings, Alfonso X appealed to James I of Aragon, whose seasoned forces subdued Murcia. The revolt permanently ended Castilian tolerance, inaugurating the widespread expulsion of Muslims from southern lands.

The uprising was ferocious: midnight daggers in town garrisons followed by merciless counter-punitive cavalry sweeps through rebel villages. No quarter was given on either side beneath the blazing Andalusian sun.

Thousands of Mudéjar peasant families fled along mountain trails toward the safety of Granada with whatever they could carry on donkey-back. Century-old irrigated fields fell barren as northern Christian settlers arrived.
